title: Maximally Extendable Sheaf Codes
text:
The recent constructions of asymptotically good classical locally testable codes (LTCs) and quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes [1,2,3,4] are all based on the idea of lifting a small local (tensor) product code to a large global code. However, for these constructions to work, it is required that the local product code has a very specific property that can be expressed topologically as a coboundary expansion of a bipartite graph with a sheaf on it [5]. When we lift the product code, its local coboundary expansion propagates to the global one [7], which implies many interesting properties of the obtained codes, including single-shot [8] linear time decoding [9,10,1], NLTS property [11], [6], and linear energy barriers [12]. Good​ qLDPC​ codes​ can​ also​ be​ converted to​ geometrically local codes [13],​ [12,14].

Sheaf theoretic approach to classical linear codes, has spurred a lot of interest recently [15,16,17], [2,5,18,19,20]. In fact, already in [15], Irit Dinur and Tali Kaufman study, in the context of property testing, the obstructions to gluing together local pieces of data into the global one, and introduced agreement tests.

In the current work, we conceptualize and generalize these ideas along with more recent research [18,19,20], and introduce a new concept that we call a sheaf code. Essentially, a sheaf code is just a specific type of Tanner code \mathcal{F}(X)=\{c\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}\mid c|_{X_{\sigma}}\in\mathcal{F}_{\sigma},\sigma\in X\} defined by a hierarchical collection of local codes \mathcal{F}_{\sigma}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{2}^{X_{\sigma}}, X_{\sigma}\subseteq[n], indexed by some poset X, playing the role of a topological space, and called its coded space. This allows one to deal with such linear codes using topological methods. In particular, it is possible to study cohomology groups H^{i}(X;\mathcal{F}) of these codes with local coefficients in \mathcal{F} (see Section VI).

The groups H^{i}(X;\mathcal{F}) are very interesting since they give us a very general way to define quantum codes out of the classical sheaf codes [18,19,20]. In fact, many existing qLDPC codes can be described in this way. For example, the famous Kitaev toric code [21] defined on the natural cellulation of a torus X=C_{\ell}\times C_{\ell}, viewed as a cell poset, where C_{\ell} is a cycle graph with \ell vertices, is H^{1}(X;\underline{\mathbb{F}_{2}}) if we denote by \underline{\mathbb{F}_{2}}(X) the constant sheaf code on X, where all local codes are repetition codes.

Another example is the codes form [4], obtained by changing the roles of checks and qubits in the expander lifted product codes [2]. These codes can be represented as H^{1}(X;\mathcal{F}), where \mathcal{F}(X)=\mathcal{A}(\Gamma)\otimes_{G}\mathcal{B}(\Gamma) is the balanced product (Definition 12) of two Zémor codes [24] \mathcal{A}(\Gamma) and \mathcal{B}(\Gamma), considered as sheaf codes on \Gamma. Note that the classical codes \mathcal{F}(X) are essentially the same as the good classical LTCs constructed in [25].

A sheaf theoretic approach to Tanner codes allows us to define a new property of such codes, that we call maximal extendibility. This idea is inspired by the notion of maximally recoverable (MR) codes [26,27], studied in the context of locally recoverable codes [28,29].

Given a sheaf code \mathcal{F}(X)\subseteq\mathbb{F}^{n}, we say that an index set U\subseteq X of local codes is extendable if every “local” codeword {c\in\mathbb{F}^{\cup_{\sigma\in U}X_{\sigma}}} satisfying only local constraints c|_{X_{\sigma}}\in\mathcal{F}_{\sigma}, {\sigma\in U}, can be extended to a “global” codeword {\hat{c}\in\mathcal{C}}, satisfying all the constraints. Furthermore, we say that \mathcal{C} is maximally extendable for a class of codes on the space X (e.g., all product codes \mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{B} with fixed dimensions of \mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}) if every set U\subseteq X extendable in some code from this class is also extendable in \mathcal{C}. As it turns out, the maximally extendable product codes have asymptotically optimal coboundary expansion properties [30] for any number of component codes. Previously this was only known in the case of two codes [4,5].

The expansion properties of product codes in more than two dimensions are very important in the context of quantum LTCs [31]. One possible way to attack the qLTC conjecture [32], [33], [20], positing the existence of good locally testable qLDPC codes (qLTCs), is to move away from the current paradigm [2,3,4,20] of defining codes on \ell -fold covering of products of graphs, to a more general paradigm of defining codes on arbitrary cubical complexes, which only locally looks like graph products. We think that an interesting direction of future research is to define sheaf codes on Ramanujan cubical complexes constructed in [34].

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. In Section II, we introduce main definitions and notations. In section III, we define sheaf codes and prove our main result. In sections IV – VII we give examples, introduce operations, and, finally, study the cohomology and the expansion of sheaf codes. We also have several appendices with some supplementary information.
